speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He said, and I quote, "This was simply untrue and not at all what was said in the interview." He said he had "never said anything about citizenship".

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He said that he did not track citizenship in his research and that his projection referred to high-net-worth individuals moving to Singapore in general, and most of them may be expatriates and work transfers, that is, not necessarily persons who applied for and became citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Different criteria may apply to different applicants, depending on their background and circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For example, an applicant applying as a spouse of a Singapore Citizen will be considered differently from someone applying on the basis of having stayed in Singapore for a period of time and contributed to employment creation in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, is there any supplementary question from you?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just a follow-up to the Minister's reply with regard to the researcher who said, as I understood Minister's reply, that it was a media publication that actually misquoted him and it sounds like a very serious case of being misquoted.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm whether MHA then reached out to the publication to enquire why the piece was eventually published as it was, in view of the sensitivity of this subject?
